title: Managing Shared Hospital Capacity for Medical Tourism: Patient Behavior, Bed Sharing, and Hybrid Simulation (simulation model)
description:
A behavior-explicit hybrid agent-based and discrete-event simulation, built in AnyLogic, of a multi-specialty international-patient hospital department that serves medical tourists and local patients from the same beds, specialists and appointment slots.

Patient behavior is part of the operational logic rather than post-hoc discussion: medication adherence, physician switching, online versus in-person channel choice, and early abandonment all feed back into flow. Compatible wards borrow each other's idle beds through inter-agent message passing, and the discrete-event layer carries visits, hospitalization, recovery and re-presentation.

Across 30 randomized-seed replications at a bed-constrained configuration, the hybrid model's mean inpatient admission waiting time is 14.8 days against 25.9 days in an otherwise identical discrete-event-only model (about 43 percent lower, p < 0.001), and the gap persists at higher demand and at larger bed counts. The difference is the contribution of the behavior and coordination layer as a whole; compatible-section bed sharing is the mechanism that acts most directly on inpatient access. The agent layer also makes patient abandonment and adherence-driven emergency escalation visible, which a pure discrete-event model omits by construction.

Requires AnyLogic 8.9.8 (Personal Learning Edition or higher). An interactive web build runs on AnyLogic Cloud without installation.
